structure: verb ない-stem + んばかりに

meaning.en: as if about to, practically doing
meaning.fr: as if about to, practically doing

examples.jp: 彼は飛び上がらんばかりに喜んだ。
examples.en: He rejoiced as if he were about to leap into the air.
examples.fr: He rejoiced as if he were about to leap into the air.

examples.jp: 彼女はあふれんばかりに涙をためていた。
examples.en: Her eyes were brimming as if the tears were about to overflow.
examples.fr: Her eyes were brimming as if the tears were about to overflow.

structure: verb dictionary form + べからず

examples.jp: この壁に落書きするべからず。
examples.en: No graffiti on this wall.
examples.fr: No graffiti on this wall.

examples.jp: ここに車を止めるべからず。
examples.en: Parking is forbidden here.
examples.fr: Parking is forbidden here.

structure: plain form/noun + ゆえに

examples.jp: 若さゆえに、彼は大きな失敗をした。
examples.en: Because of his youth, he made a big mistake.
examples.fr: Because of his youth, he made a big mistake.

examples.jp: 貧しさゆえに、学校へ通えない子どもがいる。
examples.en: There are children who cannot attend school on account of poverty.
examples.fr: There are children who cannot attend school on account of poverty.

structure: noun + なくして(は)

examples.jp: 彼の助けなくしては、この仕事は終わらなかった。
examples.en: Without his help, this work would not have been finished.
examples.fr: Without his help, this work would not have been finished.

examples.jp: 努力なくして成功はあり得ない。
examples.en: There can be no success without effort.
examples.fr: There can be no success without effort.

structure: な-adjective stem + 極まりない

examples.jp: あの店の態度は失礼極まりない。
examples.en: The attitude at that shop is extremely rude.
examples.fr: The attitude at that shop is extremely rude.

examples.jp: 危険極まりない道を、彼は一人で歩いた。
examples.en: He walked alone along an extremely dangerous road.
examples.fr: He walked alone along an extremely dangerous road.

structure: verb dictionary form/noun + の + きらいがある

examples.jp: 彼は物事を悪い方に考えるきらいがある。
examples.en: He tends to think of things in a negative way.
examples.fr: He tends to think of things in a negative way.

examples.jp: この新聞は事実を大げさに書くきらいがある。
examples.en: This newspaper has a tendency to exaggerate the facts.
examples.fr: This newspaper has a tendency to exaggerate the facts.

structure: noun + にたえない

meaning.en: can't bear to, unable to endure
meaning.fr: can't bear to, unable to endure

examples.jp: その事故の話は聞くにたえない。
examples.en: The account of that accident is unbearable to listen to.
examples.fr: The account of that accident is unbearable to listen to.

examples.jp: 彼の下品な言葉は聞くにたえなかった。
examples.en: His vulgar words were unbearable to hear.
examples.fr: His vulgar words were unbearable to hear.

structure: verb て-form + やまない

meaning.en: never stop doing, deeply and continuously
meaning.fr: never stop doing, deeply and continuously

examples.jp: 皆様のご成功を願ってやまない。
examples.en: I wish all of you success from the bottom of my heart.
examples.fr: I wish all of you success from the bottom of my heart.

examples.jp: 母は今も息子の帰りを待ってやまない。
examples.en: Even now my mother never stops waiting for her son to return.
examples.fr: Even now my mother never stops waiting for her son to return.

structure: noun + まみれ

examples.jp: 子どもたちは泥まみれになって遊んでいた。
examples.en: The children were playing covered in mud.
examples.fr: The children were playing covered in mud.

examples.jp: 彼は油まみれの手で機械を直していた。
examples.en: He was repairing the machine with oil-covered hands.
examples.fr: He was repairing the machine with oil-covered hands.

structure: verb dictionary form/noun + だに

examples.jp: そんな恐ろしいことは想像だにしなかった。
examples.en: I did not even imagine such a terrible thing.
examples.fr: I did not even imagine such a terrible thing.

examples.jp: あの日のことは、思い出すだに恐ろしい。
examples.en: Even just remembering that day is frightening.
examples.fr: Even just remembering that day is frightening.

structure: noun + あっての + noun

meaning.en: exists only thanks to, made possible by
meaning.fr: exists only thanks to, made possible by

examples.jp: お客様あっての商売だということを忘れるな。
examples.en: Do not forget that business exists only thanks to the customers.
examples.fr: Do not forget that business exists only thanks to the customers.

examples.jp: 努力あっての成功であり、運だけではない。
examples.en: Success comes only thanks to effort, not luck alone.
examples.fr: Success comes only thanks to effort, not luck alone.

structure: noun + なしに

examples.jp: 彼は何の説明もなしに会社を辞めた。
examples.en: He quit the company without any explanation at all.
examples.fr: He quit the company without any explanation at all.

examples.jp: 許しなしに部屋へ入ってはいけない。
examples.en: You must not enter the room without permission.
examples.fr: You must not enter the room without permission.

structure: noun + いかんによらず

examples.jp: 理由のいかんによらず、遅刻は認められない。
examples.en: Regardless of the reason, lateness is not accepted.
examples.fr: Regardless of the reason, lateness is not accepted.

examples.jp: 天候のいかんによらず、大会は開かれる。
examples.en: Regardless of the weather, the tournament will be held.
examples.fr: Regardless of the weather, the tournament will be held.

structure: noun + をおいて

examples.jp: この役を任せられるのは、彼をおいてほかにいない。
examples.en: There is no one but him who can be entrusted with this role.
examples.fr: There is no one but him who can be entrusted with this role.

examples.jp: この町をおいて、これほど静かな場所はない。
examples.en: There is no place as quiet as this town, other than here.
examples.fr: There is no place as quiet as this town, other than here.

structure: counter/noun + たりとも

examples.jp: 一日たりとも君のことを忘れたことはない。
examples.en: There has not been a single day I forgot about you.
examples.fr: There has not been a single day I forgot about you.

examples.jp: 一円たりともむだにはできない。
examples.en: We cannot waste even a single yen.
examples.fr: We cannot waste even a single yen.

structure: verb ない-form + までも

meaning.en: even if not quite, if not necessarily
meaning.fr: even if not quite, if not necessarily

examples.jp: 毎日とは言わないまでも、週に一度は運動したい。
examples.en: If not every day, I would like to exercise once a week.
examples.fr: If not every day, I would like to exercise once a week.

examples.jp: 完成しないまでも、ここまでは進めておきたい。
examples.en: Even if it is not finished, I want to get this far at least.
examples.fr: Even if it is not finished, I want to get this far at least.

structure: verb ない-stem + ずじまい

meaning.en: ended up never doing (despite intending to)
meaning.fr: ended up never doing (despite intending to)

examples.jp: 結局、彼には会えずじまいだった。
examples.en: In the end I never did get to meet him.
examples.fr: In the end I never did get to meet him.

examples.jp: その本は買ったのに、読まずじまいになった。
examples.en: I bought that book but ended up never reading it.
examples.fr: I bought that book but ended up never reading it.

structure: verb dictionary form + が早いか

examples.jp: 彼はベルが鳴るが早いか、教室を飛び出した。
examples.en: No sooner had the bell rung than he dashed out of the classroom.
examples.fr: No sooner had the bell rung than he dashed out of the classroom.

examples.jp: 子どもは家に着くが早いか、外へ遊びに行った。
examples.en: The moment the child got home, he went out to play.
examples.fr: The moment the child got home, he went out to play.

structure: verb dictionary form + や否や

examples.jp: 彼は席に着くや否や、話し始めた。
examples.en: No sooner had he sat down than he began to talk.
examples.fr: No sooner had he sat down than he began to talk.

examples.jp: その知らせを聞くや否や、母は泣き出した。
examples.en: The instant she heard the news, my mother burst into tears.
examples.fr: The instant she heard the news, my mother burst into tears.

structure: verb dictionary/た form + そばから

meaning.en: no sooner done than it comes undone again
meaning.fr: no sooner done than it comes undone again

examples.jp: 習ったそばから忘れてしまう。
examples.en: No sooner do I learn it than I forget it.
examples.fr: No sooner do I learn it than I forget it.

examples.jp: 片づけるそばから、子どもが部屋を散らかす。
examples.en: No sooner do I tidy up than the child messes the room again.
examples.fr: No sooner do I tidy up than the child messes the room again.

structure: verb dictionary form + なり

examples.jp: 彼は部屋に入るなり、窓を大きく開けた。
examples.en: The moment he entered the room, he threw the window wide open.
examples.fr: The moment he entered the room, he threw the window wide open.

examples.jp: 母はその手紙を読むなり、黙ってしまった。
examples.en: The instant my mother read that letter, she fell silent.
examples.fr: The instant my mother read that letter, she fell silent.

structure: verb stem / noun + がてら

meaning.en: while also, taking the chance to
meaning.fr: while also, taking the chance to

examples.jp: 散歩がてら、駅前の本屋に寄った。
examples.en: While out for a walk, I dropped by the bookshop in front of the station.
examples.fr: While out for a walk, I dropped by the bookshop in front of the station.

examples.jp: 買い物がてら、友人の家を訪ねた。
examples.en: I visited a friend while out shopping.
examples.fr: I visited a friend while out shopping.

structure: verb dictionary form / noun + の + かたわら

examples.jp: 彼は会社で働くかたわら、小説を書いている。
examples.en: Alongside working at a company, he writes novels.
examples.fr: Alongside working at a company, he writes novels.

examples.jp: 母は家事のかたわら、近所の子どもに英語を教えている。
examples.en: Alongside the housework, my mother teaches English to neighbourhood children.
examples.fr: Alongside the housework, my mother teaches English to neighbourhood children.

structure: noun + の + ごとき・ごとく

meaning.en: like, as if — an archaic ような・ように
meaning.fr: like, as if — an archaic ような・ように

examples.jp: 彼のごとき人物は、二度と現れないだろう。
examples.en: A person like him will probably never appear again.
examples.fr: A person like him will probably never appear again.

examples.jp: 時は矢のごとく過ぎていった。
examples.en: Time passed by like an arrow.
examples.fr: Time passed by like an arrow.

structure: noun + ずくめ

examples.jp: 今年はいいことずくめの一年だった。
examples.en: This year was a year full of nothing but good things.
examples.fr: This year was a year full of nothing but good things.

examples.jp: 黒ずくめの男が門の前に立っていた。
examples.en: A man dressed all in black was standing in front of the gate.
examples.fr: A man dressed all in black was standing in front of the gate.

structure: noun + めく

meaning.en: take on the air of, turn ...-like
meaning.fr: take on the air of, turn ...-like

examples.jp: 三月に入ると、日ざしが春めく。
examples.en: Once March arrives, the sunlight takes on the air of spring.
examples.fr: Once March arrives, the sunlight takes on the air of spring.

examples.jp: 彼の言い方はいつも皮肉めく。
examples.en: His way of speaking always takes on a sarcastic air.
examples.fr: His way of speaking always takes on a sarcastic air.

structure: verb dictionary form + まじき + noun

examples.jp: それは教師にあるまじき行いだ。
examples.en: That is conduct unbecoming of a teacher.
examples.fr: That is conduct unbecoming of a teacher.

examples.jp: 公務員にあるまじき発言だと批判された。
examples.en: He was criticised for a remark unbefitting a public servant.
examples.fr: He was criticised for a remark unbefitting a public servant.

structure: verb dictionary form + べく

meaning.en: in order to, so as to (formal)
meaning.fr: in order to, so as to (formal)

examples.jp: 彼は医者になるべく、必死に勉強した。
examples.en: He studied desperately in order to become a doctor.
examples.fr: He studied desperately in order to become a doctor.

examples.jp: 約束を果たすべく、彼は再びこの町に戻った。
examples.en: He returned to this town in order to fulfil his promise.
examples.fr: He returned to this town in order to fulfil his promise.

structure: verb て-form + しかるべきだ

meaning.en: ought properly to be, only right that
meaning.fr: ought properly to be, only right that

examples.jp: これだけ働いたのだから、報われてしかるべきだ。
examples.en: Having worked this much, he ought properly to be rewarded.
examples.fr: Having worked this much, he ought properly to be rewarded.

examples.jp: 被害者にはもっと説明があってしかるべきだ。
examples.en: The victims ought properly to be given more explanation.
examples.fr: The victims ought properly to be given more explanation.

structure: noun + ならでは

examples.jp: この味は、この店ならではのものだ。
examples.en: This flavour is something distinctive to this shop.
examples.fr: This flavour is something distinctive to this shop.

examples.jp: 祭りの熱気は、この町ならではだ。
examples.en: The excitement of the festival is unique to this town.
examples.fr: The excitement of the festival is unique to this town.

structure: noun / plain form + ならいざ知らず

meaning.en: I couldn't say about that, but ...
meaning.fr: I couldn't say about that, but ...

examples.jp: 子どもならいざ知らず、大人がそんなことを言うとは。
examples.en: I could not say about a child, but for an adult to say such a thing.
examples.fr: I could not say about a child, but for an adult to say such a thing.

examples.jp: 昔ならいざ知らず、今はそんなやり方は通じない。
examples.en: Perhaps in the old days, but such a method does not work now.
examples.fr: Perhaps in the old days, but such a method does not work now.

structure: plain form / noun + とはいえ

examples.jp: 春とはいえ、朝晩はまだ冷える。
examples.en: Although it is spring, mornings and evenings are still cold.
examples.fr: Although it is spring, mornings and evenings are still cold.

examples.jp: 休みとはいえ、やることが山ほどある。
examples.en: Even though it is a holiday, I have a mountain of things to do.
examples.fr: Even though it is a holiday, I have a mountain of things to do.

structure: plain form / noun + といえども

examples.jp: 子どもといえども、約束は守るべきだ。
examples.en: Even a child should keep a promise.
examples.fr: Even a child should keep a promise.

examples.jp: 専門家といえども、間違えることはある。
examples.en: Even an expert can make a mistake.
examples.fr: Even an expert can make a mistake.

structure: quoted phrase / plain form + とばかりに

meaning.en: as if to say, as though declaring
meaning.fr: as if to say, as though declaring

examples.jp: 彼は今がチャンスとばかりに立ち上がった。
examples.en: He stood up as if to say that now was his chance.
examples.fr: He stood up as if to say that now was his chance.

examples.jp: 早く帰れとばかりに、店の明かりが消された。
examples.en: The shop lights were turned off as if to say go home already.
examples.fr: The shop lights were turned off as if to say go home already.

structure: noun + をものともせず

examples.jp: 彼は足の痛みをものともせず、最後まで走り切った。
examples.en: Undaunted by the pain in his leg, he ran all the way to the end.
examples.fr: Undaunted by the pain in his leg, he ran all the way to the end.

examples.jp: 激しい風雨をものともせず、船は港を出た。
examples.en: Undaunted by the fierce wind and rain, the ship left the harbour.
examples.fr: Undaunted by the fierce wind and rain, the ship left the harbour.

structure: noun + を余儀なくされる

meaning.en: be forced into, left with no other choice
meaning.fr: be forced into, left with no other choice

examples.jp: 台風のため、大会は中止を余儀なくされた。
examples.en: Because of the typhoon, the tournament was forced into cancellation.
examples.fr: Because of the typhoon, the tournament was forced into cancellation.

examples.jp: けがのため、彼は引退を余儀なくされた。
examples.en: Owing to injury, he was forced to retire.
examples.fr: Owing to injury, he was forced to retire.

structure: noun + を皮切りに

meaning.en: starting from, with ... as the opening
meaning.fr: starting from, with ... as the opening

examples.jp: 東京を皮切りに、全国十か所で公演が行われる。
examples.en: Starting with Tokyo, performances will be held in ten places nationwide.
examples.fr: Starting with Tokyo, performances will be held in ten places nationwide.

examples.jp: その事件を皮切りに、次々と問題が明るみに出た。
examples.en: Starting with that incident, problems came to light one after another.
examples.fr: Starting with that incident, problems came to light one after another.

structure: verb dictionary form / noun + に至る

meaning.en: reach the point of, culminate in
meaning.fr: reach the point of, culminate in

examples.jp: 長い話し合いの末、ついに合意に至った。
examples.en: After long discussions, we finally reached an agreement.
examples.fr: After long discussions, we finally reached an agreement.

examples.jp: 小さな誤解が、大きな争いに至った。
examples.en: A small misunderstanding culminated in a large dispute.
examples.fr: A small misunderstanding culminated in a large dispute.

structure: noun + の極み

examples.jp: こんなに立派な賞をいただき、光栄の極みです。
examples.en: To receive such a splendid award is the height of honour.
examples.fr: To receive such a splendid award is the height of honour.

examples.jp: 連日の残業で、疲労の極みに達した。
examples.en: With overtime day after day, I reached the utmost of exhaustion.
examples.fr: With overtime day after day, I reached the utmost of exhaustion.

structure: noun + はおろか

examples.jp: 彼は漢字はおろか、ひらがなも書けない。
examples.en: Let alone kanji, he cannot even write hiragana.
examples.fr: Let alone kanji, he cannot even write hiragana.

examples.jp: 外国はおろか、隣の町へも行ったことがない。
examples.en: Let alone abroad, I have never even been to the next town.
examples.fr: Let alone abroad, I have never even been to the next town.

structure: noun + もさることながら

meaning.en: that goes without saying, but even more so
meaning.fr: that goes without saying, but even more so

examples.jp: 味もさることながら、この店は雰囲気がすばらしい。
examples.en: The taste goes without saying, but this restaurant has a wonderful atmosphere.
examples.fr: The taste goes without saying, but this restaurant has a wonderful atmosphere.

examples.jp: 値段もさることながら、品質が問題だ。
examples.en: The price goes without saying, but the quality is the real issue.
examples.fr: The price goes without saying, but the quality is the real issue.

structure: noun / question word + であれ

examples.jp: 理由が何であれ、暴力は許されない。
examples.en: Whatever the reason, violence is not permitted.
examples.fr: Whatever the reason, violence is not permitted.

examples.jp: どんな仕事であれ、全力で取り組む。
examples.en: Whatever the job, I give it everything.
examples.fr: Whatever the job, I give it everything.

structure: noun / い-adj + といったらない

examples.jp: その日の忙しさといったらなかった。
examples.en: The busyness of that day was beyond describing.
examples.fr: The busyness of that day was beyond describing.

examples.jp: あの店の対応の悪さといったらない。
examples.en: The rudeness of that shop's service is beyond words.
examples.fr: The rudeness of that shop's service is beyond words.

structure: noun + ともなると

meaning.en: once it reaches that stage, naturally
meaning.fr: once it reaches that stage, naturally

examples.jp: 責任者ともなると、休みも取れない。
examples.en: Once you become the person in charge, you can't even take a day off.
examples.fr: Once you become the person in charge, you can't even take a day off.

examples.jp: 週末ともなると、この道は大変込む。
examples.en: Come the weekend, this road gets terribly crowded.
examples.fr: Come the weekend, this road gets terribly crowded.

structure: verb dictionary form + ともなく

examples.jp: 見るともなく窓の外をながめていた。
examples.en: I was gazing absently out of the window.
examples.fr: I was gazing absently out of the window.

examples.jp: 聞くともなく聞いた話が、後で役に立った。
examples.en: Something I overheard without listening came in useful later.
examples.fr: Something I overheard without listening came in useful later.

structure: verb stem + つ + opposite verb stem + つ

examples.jp: 二人の走者は、抜きつ抜かれつの接戦だった。
examples.en: The two runners fought it out, first one ahead and then the other.
examples.fr: The two runners fought it out, first one ahead and then the other.

examples.jp: 駅前を行きつ戻りつして、彼を待った。
examples.en: I paced back and forth outside the station waiting for him.
examples.fr: I paced back and forth outside the station waiting for him.

structure: verb ない-stem + んがため

examples.jp: 生きんがために、彼は必死で働いた。
examples.en: He worked desperately in order to live.
examples.fr: He worked desperately in order to live.

examples.jp: 勝たんがための努力が実を結んだ。
examples.en: The effort made purely in order to win bore fruit.
examples.fr: The effort made purely in order to win bore fruit.

structure: verb dictionary form + べくもない

meaning.en: there is no possibility of it whatever
meaning.fr: there is no possibility of it whatever

examples.jp: この結果は、だれにも予想すべくもなかった。
examples.en: This outcome was something nobody could possibly have foreseen.
examples.fr: This outcome was something nobody could possibly have foreseen.

examples.jp: 素人の私には、比べるべくもない。
examples.en: For an amateur like me, there is no comparison to be made.
examples.fr: For an amateur like me, there is no comparison to be made.

structure: verb dictionary form + すべがない

examples.jp: 連絡先を知らないので、知らせるすべがない。
examples.en: I do not know how to reach them, so there is no way of telling them.
examples.fr: I do not know how to reach them, so there is no way of telling them.

examples.jp: 今となっては、確かめるすべがない。
examples.en: At this point there is no means left of checking.
examples.fr: At this point there is no means left of checking.

structure: plain form / noun + の + こととて

meaning.en: seeing that it is so, formally offered
meaning.fr: seeing that it is so, formally offered

examples.jp: 慣れぬこととて、失礼があったかもしれません。
examples.en: Being unaccustomed to it, I may have been rude.
examples.fr: Being unaccustomed to it, I may have been rude.

examples.jp: 急なこととて、十分な用意ができませんでした。
examples.en: It being so sudden, I could not prepare properly.
examples.fr: It being so sudden, I could not prepare properly.

structure: plain form / noun + とあって

meaning.en: the situation being what it is
meaning.fr: the situation being what it is

examples.jp: 連休とあって、どこも人でいっぱいだ。
examples.en: It being a long weekend, everywhere is packed.
examples.fr: It being a long weekend, everywhere is packed.

examples.jp: 有名な歌手が来るとあって、会場は満員だ。
examples.en: With a famous singer coming, the hall is full.
examples.fr: With a famous singer coming, the hall is full.

structure: plain form / noun + とあれば

meaning.en: if that is truly the case, then
meaning.fr: if that is truly the case, then

examples.jp: 子どものためとあれば、どんな苦労もいとわない。
examples.en: If it is for my child, I will bear any hardship.
examples.fr: If it is for my child, I will bear any hardship.

examples.jp: 必要とあれば、すぐにでも向かいます。
examples.en: If it proves necessary, I will set off at once.
examples.fr: If it proves necessary, I will set off at once.

structure: noun + たるもの

meaning.en: one who holds that position ought to
meaning.fr: one who holds that position ought to

examples.jp: 教師たるもの、常に学び続けるべきだ。
examples.en: One who is a teacher ought always to go on learning.
examples.fr: One who is a teacher ought always to go on learning.

examples.jp: 責任者たるもの、逃げてはならない。
examples.en: A person in charge must not run away.
examples.fr: A person in charge must not run away.

structure: noun + にして

meaning.en: only at that stage; also: being that very thing
meaning.fr: only at that stage; also: being that very thing

examples.jp: 百歳にして、なお創作を続けている。
examples.en: At a hundred years of age, he is still creating.
examples.fr: At a hundred years of age, he is still creating.

examples.jp: 三度目にして、ようやく成功した。
examples.en: It was only on the third attempt that it finally succeeded.
examples.fr: It was only on the third attempt that it finally succeeded.

structure: noun + にあって

examples.jp: この厳しい状況にあって、彼は冷静だった。
examples.en: Placed in these harsh circumstances, he stayed calm.
examples.fr: Placed in these harsh circumstances, he stayed calm.

examples.jp: 戦後の混乱期にあって、人々は助け合った。
examples.en: In the chaos of the postwar years, people helped one another.
examples.fr: In the chaos of the postwar years, people helped one another.

structure: noun + をよそに

examples.jp: 親の心配をよそに、彼は旅に出た。
examples.en: Paying no heed to his parents' worry, he set off travelling.
examples.fr: Paying no heed to his parents' worry, he set off travelling.

examples.jp: 周囲の反対をよそに、計画は進められた。
examples.en: In disregard of the opposition around it, the plan went ahead.
examples.fr: In disregard of the opposition around it, the plan went ahead.

structure: noun + かたがた

meaning.en: and taking the occasion to, formally
meaning.fr: and taking the occasion to, formally

examples.jp: お礼かたがた、ごあいさつに伺いました。
examples.en: I have called to pay my respects and to thank you.
examples.fr: I have called to pay my respects and to thank you.

examples.jp: 散歩かたがた、郵便局に寄ってきた。
examples.en: I dropped by the post office while out for a walk.
examples.fr: I dropped by the post office while out for a walk.

structure: plain form + しまつだ

meaning.en: and it came to this sorry pass
meaning.fr: and it came to this sorry pass

examples.jp: 何度も注意したのに、とうとうけんかを始めるしまつだ。
examples.en: I warned him again and again, and in the end he started a fight.
examples.fr: I warned him again and again, and in the end he started a fight.

examples.jp: 遅刻を重ねたあげく、だまって休むしまつだ。
examples.en: After repeated lateness, it came to him taking days off without a word.
examples.fr: After repeated lateness, it came to him taking days off without a word.

structure: verb ない-stem + ずにはおかない

meaning.en: it cannot but bring that about
meaning.fr: it cannot but bring that about

examples.jp: あの映画は、見る者を感動させずにはおかない。
examples.en: That film cannot fail to move those who see it.
examples.fr: That film cannot fail to move those who see it.

examples.jp: この発言は、議論を呼ばずにはおかないだろう。
examples.en: This remark is bound to provoke debate.
examples.fr: This remark is bound to provoke debate.

structure: verb て-form + はばからない

meaning.en: says or does it without a qualm
meaning.fr: says or does it without a qualm

examples.jp: 彼は自分が一番だと言ってはばからない。
examples.en: He says without a qualm that he is the best.
examples.fr: He says without a qualm that he is the best.

examples.jp: その政治家は批判を口にしてはばからない。
examples.en: That politician voices criticism without hesitation.
examples.fr: That politician voices criticism without hesitation.

structure: noun + なりに

meaning.en: in the way proper to what it is
meaning.fr: in the way proper to what it is

examples.jp: 子どもは子どもなりに、よく考えている。
examples.en: Children think it through in their own childlike way.
examples.fr: Children think it through in their own childlike way.

examples.jp: 私なりに努力したつもりです。
examples.en: I did make an effort, in my own way.
examples.fr: I did make an effort, in my own way.

structure: noun / verb stem + ながらに

examples.jp: 彼女は涙ながらに、当時のことを語った。
examples.en: She spoke of those days with tears in her eyes.
examples.fr: She spoke of those days with tears in her eyes.

examples.jp: 生まれながらに、すぐれた才能を持っていた。
examples.en: He possessed outstanding talent from birth.
examples.fr: He possessed outstanding talent from birth.

structure: noun / verb dictionary form + にかたくない

examples.jp: 彼の失望は想像にかたくない。
examples.en: His disappointment is not hard to imagine.
examples.fr: His disappointment is not hard to imagine.

examples.jp: 結果は予想にかたくなかった。
examples.en: The outcome was easy enough to predict.
examples.fr: The outcome was easy enough to predict.

structure: noun + にとどまらず

meaning.en: and it does not stop there
meaning.fr: and it does not stop there

examples.jp: 被害は一つの町にとどまらず、県全体に広がった。
examples.en: The damage was not confined to one town but spread across the prefecture.
examples.fr: The damage was not confined to one town but spread across the prefecture.

examples.jp: 彼の活動は国内にとどまらず、海外にも及ぶ。
examples.en: His work does not stop at home but extends abroad.
examples.fr: His work does not stop at home but extends abroad.

structure: noun / plain form + の + にひきかえ

examples.jp: 兄が明るいのにひきかえ、弟は口が重い。
examples.en: In contrast to his cheerful older brother, the younger one is taciturn.
examples.fr: In contrast to his cheerful older brother, the younger one is taciturn.

examples.jp: 去年の不作にひきかえ、今年は豊作だ。
examples.en: Set against last year's poor harvest, this year's is abundant.
examples.fr: Set against last year's poor harvest, this year's is abundant.

structure: plain form + のなんのって

examples.jp: あの日の寒さのなんのって、耳が痛かった。
examples.en: The cold that day was something else; my ears hurt.
examples.fr: The cold that day was something else; my ears hurt.

examples.jp: その量のなんのって、とても食べきれない。
examples.en: The sheer quantity was absurd; I could never finish it.
examples.fr: The sheer quantity was absurd; I could never finish it.

structure: noun + はさておき

examples.jp: 費用のことはさておき、まず計画を立てよう。
examples.en: Leaving the cost aside for now, let's first make a plan.
examples.fr: Leaving the cost aside for now, let's first make a plan.

examples.jp: 冗談はさておき、本題に入りましょう。
examples.en: Joking aside, let us get to the main point.
examples.fr: Joking aside, let us get to the main point.

structure: verb dictionary form + までのことだ

meaning.en: then that is all there is to do
meaning.fr: then that is all there is to do

examples.jp: だめなら、また一からやり直すまでのことだ。
examples.en: If it fails, we simply start again from scratch.
examples.fr: If it fails, we simply start again from scratch.

examples.jp: 断られたら、他をあたるまでのことだ。
examples.en: If they refuse, we just try somewhere else.
examples.fr: If they refuse, we just try somewhere else.

structure: emotion noun + を禁じ得ない

meaning.en: one cannot hold the feeling back
meaning.fr: one cannot hold the feeling back

examples.jp: その知らせに、驚きを禁じ得なかった。
examples.en: I could not suppress my astonishment at the news.
examples.fr: I could not suppress my astonishment at the news.

examples.jp: あの光景には、涙を禁じ得ない。
examples.en: One cannot hold back tears at that sight.
examples.fr: One cannot hold back tears at that sight.

structure: verb ば-form + こそ

meaning.en: it is only because of that
meaning.fr: it is only because of that

examples.jp: 君のことを思えばこそ、厳しく言うのだ。
examples.en: It is precisely because I care about you that I speak harshly.
examples.fr: It is precisely because I care about you that I speak harshly.

examples.jp: 努力があればこそ、今の成功がある。
examples.en: It is only because of the effort that today's success exists.
examples.fr: It is only because of the effort that today's success exists.

structure: verb volitional form + が + verb dictionary form + まいが

examples.jp: みんなが信じようが信じまいが、これは事実だ。
examples.en: Whether everyone believes it or not, this is a fact.
examples.fr: Whether everyone believes it or not, this is a fact.

examples.jp: 彼が来ようが来まいが、私は始める。
examples.en: Whether he comes or not, I shall begin.
examples.fr: Whether he comes or not, I shall begin.
